Commentary.Commentary: India on top - For now, India Women go top of Group A, thanks to a superior run-rate, but both India and Australia are looking in prime form and the frontrunners in the race for the semi-finals. Next up, we have the chasing pack playing in the third and final game of the day. South Africa Women take on Pakistan Women in Birmingham, and Pakistan have decided to bat first in that clash. You can simply switch tabs and tune in to our coverage of that game, which is about to start at 5.30 pm GMT (11 pm IST). Cheers!

The skipper of India Women - Harmanpreet Kaur says that they were really good with the bat. Adds that it wasn't easy conditions to bat, but the way Smriti and Shafali batted, it set the tone for them. Mentions that Shafali Verma is always ready to bowl whenever the team needs and hopefully she can keep getting the breakthroughs and maybe become a good all-rounder in the future. Kaur shares that she doesn't have an exact update about Shreyanka Patil, but the medical team is looking after her and will provide an update soon. She reckons that they are in a really good position as a team and hopefully they continue to play good cricket as the tournament progresses. Kaur ends by praising the two seamers. Says that Kranti Gaud has been good with the new ball, while Nandni Sharma has used her experience of WPL here as well.

The captain of Netherlands Women - Babette de Leede says that India batted really well, especially up front, but her team came back well with the ball. Reckons they had a chance on this flat wicket, but failed to capitalize with the bat. On the catching, she says that it could have been better, and also with the ball they could have avoided so many extras. On Caroline de Lange, she says that Caroline bowled well and the opposition just played smart cricket, which they can learn from.

POTM - Smriti Mandhana is adjudged the Player of the Match for her brilliant knock of 74 runs. Smriti says that it was a good batting wicket. Adds that she has played a few matches here in Leeds in the Hundred and it is always a good batting wicket and quick outfield, but also credits Netherlands Women for their effort. Mentions that they didn't know much about the Dutch before the game and watched a lot of videos for the preparation but also appreciate the opponents for the way they fielded and bowled. Says it was about sticking to their strength and doing the job for the team. Shares that she didn't middle the ball as she would have liked in her innings and it is still a work in progress, but she wants to keep improving every game.
The Presentation ceremony...

Recapping the first innings - Babette de Leede opted to bowl first under overcast conditions as Netherlands Women looked to keep the Indian batters in check. However, this backfired and the Indian openers put on a 115-run stand. The Dutch bowlers bowled too many extras up front as both Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana notched up their individual fifties. Netherlands Women did come back well with the ball but India Women managed to cross the 200 run barrier thanks to their batting depth.

The Dutch show sparks of brilliance - The scoreline might depict a huge loss but for a long while, Netherlands Women's top order took the fight to the Indian bowlers. Babette de Leede and Sterre Kalis held the fort down in the middle overs but once the top order got out, things started to fall apart. They went from 113/5 to 114 all out, something they will look to rectify soon.

Nearly perfect - India Women have now won two games on the trot by huge margins and seem like a well-oiled unit, but that injury to Shreyanka Patil is something they wouldn't have wanted, especially so early in the tournament. With the ball, the pacers were decent but Nandni Sharma did show some sparks on her World Cup debut, but the spinners were the stars of the show. Sree Charani picked up four wickets and Shafali Verma too contributed with three wickets, who was given an extended spell after that injury to Patil.

India flex their muscles - Well, that was a quick end to the Netherlands Women innings and India Women have made it two wins out of two to kickstart their World Cup campaign. The reigning ODI World Champions are looking as one of the sides to beat in the shortest format of the game as well.

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, that doesn't look good. Shreyanka Patil is down, holding her right ankle and seems to be in a lot of pain. The physio comes out to have a look and the umpires decide to take a DRINKS break as well. So far, so good for India Women, but Netherlands Women have shown good intent and have put away the bad balls. Heather Siegers in particular seemed to be striking the ball well, but she's departed now and the Indians will look to employ the spinners and try and choke the Dutch batters through the middle phase. Uh, uh! It seems like Shreyanka Patil's game, or even her campaign, might be cut short here. She simply isn't able to put any weight on that foot and there is a buggy out on the ground to carry her off the field. Very unfortunate for Patil, and also India. Hopefully, she gets fine real soon. Patil is off the field and it will be Shafali Verma to complete here over. Also, Radha Yadav is on as the substitute fielder.

Floated, full and on middle, Phebe Molkenboer stays back and tucks it to the right of short mid-wicket. The fielder runs to her left but only parries it away.
